940GZZLUSJP.funFact: The station is built into 55 Broadway, Charles Holden's 1929 Underground headquarters that was then the tallest office block in London and carries sculptures by Epstein, Gill and others.

940GZZLUSJW.name: St. John's Wood Underground Station
940GZZLUSJW.funFact: It is the nearest Tube station to both Lord's Cricket Ground and the Abbey Road zebra crossing the Beatles made famous.

940GZZLUSKS.name: South Kensington Underground Station
940GZZLUSKS.funFact: An 1885 tiled pedestrian subway, still in use today, runs from the station beneath Exhibition Road, giving sheltered access towards the Natural History, Science and V&A museums.

940GZZLUSKT.name: South Kenton Underground Station
940GZZLUSKT.funFact: South Kenton opened in 1933 as a late addition to the London and North Western Railway's 'New Line' from Euston to Watford, which had opened in 1912, once the local population had grown enough to justify a stop.

940GZZLUSKW.name: Stockwell Underground Station
940GZZLUSKW.funFact: A WWII deep-level shelter sits beneath Stockwell, its surface rotunda now a war memorial.

940GZZLUSNB.name: Snaresbrook Underground Station
940GZZLUSNB.funFact: The station borders a detached portion of Epping Forest by Eagle Pond, formerly Snares Pond, whose name is sometimes linked to snares once set to trap animals or birds in the forest, though the origin is uncertain.

940GZZLUSPU.name: St. Paul's Underground Station
940GZZLUSPU.funFact: St Paul's, beside Wren's cathedral, was renamed from 'Post Office' in 1937.

940GZZLUSRP.name: South Ruislip Underground Station
940GZZLUSRP.funFact: The rounded booking hall holds a frieze of concrete, glass and granite chips that is one of the earliest public works by the glass artist Henry Haig.

940GZZLUSSQ.name: Sloane Square Underground Station
940GZZLUSSQ.funFact: A large iron pipe slung above the platforms carries the buried River Westbourne over the tracks, a Victorian solution still in place since the station opened in 1868.

940GZZLUSTD.name: Stratford Underground Station
940GZZLUSTD.funFact: Stratford was the gateway to the 2012 Olympic Park.

940GZZLUSTM.name: Stanmore Underground Station
940GZZLUSTM.funFact: Stanmore opened in 1932 as the Metropolitan Railway's terminus of a branch from Wembley Park, later passing to the Bakerloo line in 1939 and then to the Jubilee line in 1979.

940GZZLUSUH.name: Sudbury Hill Underground Station
940GZZLUSUH.funFact: Sudbury Hill is a smaller red-brick version of Charles Holden's 'brick box with a concrete lid' that he pioneered at neighbouring Sudbury Town.

940GZZLUSUT.name: Sudbury Town Underground Station
940GZZLUSUT.funFact: Sudbury Town set the template for Charles Holden's 1930s 'brick box with a concrete lid' stations.

940GZZLUSVS.name: Seven Sisters Underground Station
940GZZLUSVS.funFact: The name comes from a ring of seven elm trees planted around a central walnut on Page Green in Tottenham, a clump recorded as the Seven Sisters by 1732.

940GZZLUSWC.name: Swiss Cottage Underground Station
940GZZLUSWC.funFact: The station is named after a chalet-style pub built around 1804 as the Swiss Tavern at the road junction above, later called Ye Olde Swiss Cottage, which closed in early 2025.

940GZZLUSWF.name: South Woodford Underground Station
940GZZLUSWF.funFact: The station sits beside Charlie Brown's Roundabout, named after the landlord of a pub called The Roundabout that was demolished in 1972 to make way for M11 slip roads.

940GZZLUSWK.name: Southwark Underground Station
940GZZLUSWK.funFact: Its concourse holds a 40 metre curved wall of 660 pieces of blue glass by Alexander Beleschenko, inspired by Schinkel's set design for The Magic Flute.

940GZZLUSWN.name: South Wimbledon Underground Station
940GZZLUSWN.funFact: Charles Holden's station actually stands in Merton, but was named South Wimbledon because Wimbledon was reckoned the more genteel address.

940GZZLUTAW.name: Totteridge & Whetstone Underground Station
940GZZLUTAW.funFact: Whetstone is reputedly where soldiers sharpened their blades before the 1471 Battle of Barnet, though the name predates the battle, so the tale is folklore.

940GZZLUTBC.name: Tooting Bec Underground Station
940GZZLUTBC.funFact: The Bec recalls Bec Abbey in Normandy, which held the manor, and nearby Tooting Bec Lido is the largest freshwater pool by surface area in the UK.

940GZZLUTBY.name: Tooting Broadway Underground Station
940GZZLUTBY.funFact: A bronze statue of King Edward VII, erected by public subscription and unveiled in 1911, stands just outside the station.

940GZZLUTCR.name: Tottenham Court Road Underground Station
940GZZLUTCR.funFact: Tottenham Court Road is lined with Eduardo Paolozzi's vivid 1980s mosaics.

940GZZLUTFP.name: Tufnell Park Underground Station
940GZZLUTFP.funFact: The district and station are named after William Tufnell, who was granted the manor of Barnsbury in 1753.

940GZZLUTHB.name: Theydon Bois Underground Station
940GZZLUTHB.funFact: The 'Bois' comes from the medieval de Bois family who held the manor, and a parish clerk reputedly recommended the French spelling for the village's forest setting.

940GZZLUTMH.name: Tottenham Hale Underground Station
940GZZLUTMH.funFact: 'Hale' is traditionally said to derive from an Old English word for hoisting, marking where goods such as timber were unloaded from boats on the River Lea.

940GZZLUTMP.name: Temple Underground Station
940GZZLUTMP.funFact: Temple takes its name from the medieval Temple and the Inns of Court above it.

940GZZLUTNG.name: Turnham Green Underground Station
940GZZLUTNG.funFact: The 1642 Battle of Turnham Green, a Civil War standoff that turned Charles I back from London, was fought across open fields near here now built over by Chiswick.

940GZZLUTPN.name: Turnpike Lane Underground Station
940GZZLUTPN.funFact: It is named after a toll gate erected on Green Lanes in 1765 by the Stamford Hill and Green Lanes Turnpike Trust.

940GZZLUTWH.name: Tower Hill Underground Station
940GZZLUTWH.funFact: Tower Hill is the stop for the Tower of London and Tower Bridge.

940GZZLUUPB.name: Upminster Bridge Underground Station
940GZZLUUPB.funFact: A large reversed swastika, an innocent good-luck motif when laid in 1934, is tiled into the floor of the station's ticket hall.

940GZZLUUPK.name: Upton Park Underground Station
940GZZLUUPK.funFact: It is the local stop for West Ham United's old Boleyn Ground, which took its name from the adjacent Green Street House, reputedly linked by local legend to Anne Boleyn, and which the club called home until 2016.

940GZZLUUPM.name: Upminster Underground Station
940GZZLUUPM.funFact: A short walk away stands Upminster Windmill, a Grade II* listed smock mill built in 1803 and widely regarded as one of the finest surviving English smock mills.

940GZZLUUPY.name: Upney Underground Station
940GZZLUUPY.funFact: The station takes its name from Upney Lane in Barking, and the old place name is usually read as a 'higher' patch of dry ground or island in the marshes, from the Old English element 'eg'.

940GZZLUUXB.name: Uxbridge Underground Station
940GZZLUUXB.funFact: Charles Holden's 1938 station is Grade II listed and lit by stained glass by the Hungarian artist Ervin Bossanyi showing the heraldry of Middlesex and Buckinghamshire.

940GZZLUVIC.name: Victoria Underground Station
940GZZLUVIC.funFact: One of the Underground's busiest stations, it sits east of Buckingham Palace Road and just south of Victoria Street, from which it takes its name.

940GZZLUVXL.name: Vauxhall Underground Station
940GZZLUVXL.funFact: Vauxhall is often credited as the origin of the Russian word for a railway station, 'vokzal'.

940GZZLUWAF.name: Watford Underground Station
940GZZLUWAF.funFact: This Metropolitan line terminus sits in the Cassiobury area close to the park, about a mile from the town centre it was once marketed to reach as part of Metro-land.

940GZZLUWBN.name: West Brompton Underground Station
940GZZLUWBN.funFact: The station sits beside the Victorian Brompton Cemetery, one of London's 'Magnificent Seven', and close to Chelsea FC's Stamford Bridge stadium.

940GZZLUWCY.name: White City Underground Station
940GZZLUWCY.funFact: It is named after the gleaming white-clad buildings of the 1908 Franco-British Exhibition, whose stadium hosted that year's Olympic Games.

940GZZLUWFN.name: West Finchley Underground Station
940GZZLUWFN.funFact: The station opened in 1933 fitted with second-hand materials from closed northern railways, and its footbridge is said to have come from a Yorkshire colliery line, though which station it came from is disputed.

940GZZLUWHM.name: West Ham Underground Station
940GZZLUWHM.funFact: Comprehensively rebuilt for the 1999 Jubilee line extension to a design evoking Charles Holden's 1930s work, it was by far the cheapest of the new stations on that line.

940GZZLUWHP.name: West Hampstead Underground Station
940GZZLUWHP.funFact: It is one of three separate stations strung along West End Lane within about 200 metres, serving the Jubilee line, the Overground and Thameslink.

940GZZLUWHW.name: West Harrow Underground Station
940GZZLUWHW.funFact: It opened in 1913 as a wooden halt after residents of the growing Bessborough Estate pressed the Metropolitan Railway to add a stop on its line towards Uxbridge.

940GZZLUWIG.name: Willesden Green Underground Station
940GZZLUWIG.funFact: Its cream faience station buildings, dating from a 1925 rebuild by Metropolitan Railway architect C. W. Clark and retaining original mosaic tiling, helped earn the station its Grade II listing.

940GZZLUWIM.name: Wimbledon Underground Station
940GZZLUWIM.funFact: Wimbledon, a District line terminus, is home to the tennis championships.

940GZZLUWIP.name: Wimbledon Park Underground Station
940GZZLUWIP.funFact: It is one of three District line stops serving the All England Lawn Tennis Club, about a 25 minute walk from the Wimbledon Championships courts.

940GZZLUWJN.name: Willesden Junction Underground Station
940GZZLUWJN.funFact: In the late nineteenth century its maze of platforms and passages earned it the nickname 'Bewildering Junction', and it sits beside Old Oak Common, where HS2's new interchange is being built.

940GZZLUWKA.name: Warwick Avenue Underground Station
940GZZLUWKA.funFact: It serves Little Venice, the canal pool often linked to the poet Robert Browning, who lived nearby; the avenue itself is said to be named after Jane Warwick of Warwick Hall near Carlisle.

940GZZLUWKN.name: West Kensington Underground Station
940GZZLUWKN.funFact: It opened on the District Railway in 1874 as 'North End (Fulham)' and was renamed West Kensington in 1877, with its entrance later rebuilt to a Charles Holden design.

940GZZLUWLA.name: Wood Lane Underground Station
940GZZLUWLA.funFact: Opened in 2008 to serve Westfield London, it was the first wholly new station built on an existing Tube line in over 70 years, the previous one being Elm Park in 1935.

940GZZLUWLO.name: Waterloo Underground Station
940GZZLUWLO.funFact: Waterloo is served by the Waterloo & City line, the little shuttle Londoners nickname 'the Drain'.

940GZZLUWOF.name: Woodford Underground Station
940GZZLUWOF.funFact: Winston Churchill represented this constituency as an MP for around 40 years, and a bronze statue of him by David McFall, unveiled in 1959, stands on nearby Woodford Green.

940GZZLUWOG.name: Wood Green Underground Station
940GZZLUWOG.funFact: A Charles Holden design from the 1932 Piccadilly line Cockfosters extension, it is the closest Tube station to Alexandra Palace, where the BBC began its television service in 1936.

940GZZLUWOP.name: Woodside Park Underground Station
940GZZLUWOP.funFact: This country-style station keeps a Victorian VR postbox set into its front wall and lies beside the Dollis Brook in leafy Barnet.

940GZZLUWPL.name: Whitechapel Underground Station
940GZZLUWPL.funFact: Its Whitechapel Road entrance dates from the 1876 railway station, and the nearby Royal London Hospital cared for Joseph Merrick, the 'Elephant Man', until his death in 1890.

940GZZLUWRP.name: West Ruislip Underground Station
940GZZLUWRP.funFact: It is the western terminus of the Central line, where the Underground shares the site with Chiltern Railways trains running out towards Buckinghamshire.

940GZZLUWRR.name: Warren Street Underground Station
940GZZLUWRR.funFact: Its Victoria line platforms carry a maze tile motif by the Crosby/Fletcher/Forbes design partnership, a visual pun on the 'warren' in the station's name.

940GZZLUWSD.name: Wanstead Underground Station
940GZZLUWSD.funFact: Wanstead's unopened Central line tunnels hid a secret aircraft-parts factory during WWII.

940GZZLUWSM.name: Westminster Underground Station
940GZZLUWSM.funFact: Westminster's deep station box sits beneath Portcullis House, right by Parliament and Big Ben.

940GZZLUWSP.name: Westbourne Park Underground Station
940GZZLUWSP.funFact: It has an eastbound platform exit onto Tavistock Crescent that opens during the Notting Hill Carnival to move large crowds out of the station quickly.

940GZZLUWTA.name: West Acton Underground Station
940GZZLUWTA.funFact: Its Grade II listed building is the only station completed to the original design of Australian-born GWR architect Brian Lewis, opened in 1940 as part of the New Works Programme.

940GZZLUWWL.name: Walthamstow Central Underground Station
940GZZLUWWL.funFact: Walthamstow Central, the Victoria line's northern terminus, is near the William Morris Gallery.

940GZZLUWYC.name: Wembley Central Underground Station
940GZZLUWYC.funFact: Linked to Wembley Stadium by the White Horse Bridge, it was renamed from 'Wembley for Sudbury' to Wembley Central in 1948, the year London hosted the Olympic Games.

940GZZLUWYP.name: Wembley Park Underground Station
940GZZLUWYP.funFact: Wembley Park is the stop for Wembley Stadium.

940GZZNEUGST.name: Nine Elms Underground Station
940GZZNEUGST.funFact: Opened in 2021 on the Northern line extension, it serves the US Embassy and takes its name from a row of elm trees recorded along the lane around 1645.
